about.title: About
paragraphs: Biomedical engineering introduced me to programming, signal processing, electronics, medical science, CAD and simulation. Programming felt familiar because it reminded me of drawing. You begin with an empty space then build something useful from it.

Curiosity led me toward computational imaging. The deeper I went, the more I enjoyed learning how light behaves and how polarization, Jones matrices and hologram reconstruction can reveal information that ordinary images miss.
I also want to turn novel ideas into useful products and sustainable ventures. For me that starts with understanding the problem, studying it properly and building with purpose.

researchExperience.title: Graduate Researcher - Biomedical Optics & Computational Imaging
bullets: Developed a polarization-sensitive DHM system and Python pipeline for FFT hologram reconstruction, phase processing, full-field Jones matrix reconstruction, retardance and fast-axis analysis.

Led the end-to-end experimental workflow in collaboration with my academic advisor, including system design and setup, equipment planning, camera configuration, experiments, image processing, validation, visualization and manuscript preparation.
Published a dual-shot phase-bias equalization method validated with birefringent film and applied to mouse brain and human cornea samples.

research.title: Featured research
research.paperTitle: Dual-shot polarization digital holographic microscopy with phase bias equalization for full-field Jones matrix imaging
research.citation: Mohammad M. T. R. Hussein and M. Fatih Toy · Biomedical Optics Express 17, 1877–1896 · 2026
research.explanation: Sequential hologram acquisitions can introduce phase differences that reduce Jones matrix accuracy. This work presents a dual-shot PDHM system that uses isotropic reference regions to correct inter-shot phase bias. It was validated with birefringent film and applied to mouse brain and human cornea samples.
research.limitation: The published method requires an isotropic reference region and is intended for static or quasi-static samples.

projects.title: Dual-shot PDHM
projects.summary: Full-field Jones matrix imaging with inter-shot phase bias equalization.
projects.role: Led the end-to-end research workflow while collaborating with my academic advisor. This included system design, setup, purchasing, camera configuration, processing, experiments, validation, visualization and writing.
projects.problem: Sequential polarization measurements contain relative phase offsets. Once the Jones matrix is reconstructed, those offsets can produce large errors in the recovered polarization information.
projects.process: Designed a dual-shot optical configuration and a Python reconstruction pipeline covering FFT filtering, phase reconstruction, unwrapping, correction, retardance and optical-axis analysis.
projects.outcome: Equalized inter-shot phase bias through isotropic reference regions, validated the method with birefringent film and demonstrated full-field imaging on mouse brain and human cornea samples.

projects.title: Reference-Free Phase Bias Equalization
projects.summary: An optimization-based approach that removes the need for an isotropic reference region.
projects.role: Designed the approach, built the processing workflow, tested the method, analyzed the results and completed the manuscript draft in collaboration with my academic advisor.
projects.problem: The first method depends on finding an isotropic reference region. Some samples do not provide one, which limits where the correction can be used.
projects.process: Formulated phase bias as an optimization problem and evaluated whether the Jones matrix can be corrected without a sample reference region.
projects.outcome: Completed an optimization-based reference-free method and a full manuscript draft. The work is not yet submitted or published.

projects.title: Patient-Specific Knee Reconstruction & FEA
projects.summary: Patient-specific knee models, an implant concept and comparative structural simulations.
projects.role: Official TÜBİTAK 2209-A Project Partner. I handled the research, image processing, 3D reconstruction, implant concepts, simulation work, report preparation and much of the team coordination.
projects.problem: Explore how patient imaging and computational simulation can support the comparison of knee-replacement design ideas.
projects.process: Studied CT, MRI and DICOM data, reconstructed multiple patient knees in 3D Slicer, designed implant concepts in Fusion 360 and compared static structural behavior using FEA tools including ANSYS.
projects.outcome: Reconstructed patient-specific knee models, proposed a new implant concept and completed FEA comparisons covering deformation, displacement and von Mises stress. The work was computational and not clinically validated.

projects.title: VitroMech

projects.role: Co-founder focused on software and technical development as well as the orthopedics direction.
projects.problem: Explore a clearer workflow for turning medical imaging into patient-specific 3D anatomical models for research and visualization.
projects.process: Developed the early product direction, technical concept and public website around DICOM segmentation and anatomical modeling.
projects.outcome: Built and presented an early startup concept. The startup is currently paused and no clinical outcomes are claimed.

projects.title: Workin

projects.role: Created the product, structured its training flow and built the complete public experience.
projects.problem: Make structured at-home calisthenics easier to follow without turning the workout into another complicated dashboard.
projects.process: Designed a mobile-first flow around a four-week plan, daily exercise logging, rest timing, notes and downloadable workout material.
projects.outcome: Delivered a public tracker with day and week progress, rest timers, notes and downloadable plans.

projects.title: Salat Plans
projects.summary: A task planner that organizes daily priorities around prayer times.
projects.role: Created the product concept, experience and complete public application.
projects.problem: Daily plans often ignore the fixed moments that already give the day structure.
projects.process: Designed a calm planning flow that places tasks between prayer times and supports recovery after missed days without shame-based streaks.
projects.outcome: Released a working local-first planner with prayer-based time blocks and a focused daily planning experience.
